findings.finding: Native error lists coalesce repeated domain violations and silently truncate at the cutoff.
findings.disposition: Independent signed/absolute error expectations and cutoff probes document native behavior; Rust reports every rejected occurrence or fails the entire transaction before publication.

findings.finding: Sorting by keys plus typed values can change the surviving duplicate.
findings.disposition: Global input ordinal precedes value/provenance payload. Domain checks precede duplicates; first valid input wins, including scalars. Tests retain bit-exact rejected values and ordinals.

findings.finding: Replay and symbol-initialization failures can discard secondary cursor/sorter cleanup errors, or overwrite the primary failure after metadata cleanup.
findings.disposition: Explicit close/cancel before parent cleanup, internal nonterminal symbol initialization while sorter exists, conditional post-error statistics and primary-error retention. Writer.fail now retains the first attached cursor cleanup diagnostic even when parent cleanup also fails, while still attempting parent cleanup and retaining retry ownership. Fault regressions cover callback refusal, initialization output limit, secondary cursor denial, parent denial and abort retry.

findings.finding: Forward registration changes symbol IDs and physical data order; it must preserve direct alias identity.
findings.disposition: Two independent complete metadata/record recipes cover both registration layouts in native readers, including forward name references. Dependency scheduling never renumbers registered symbols.

findings.finding: Unbounded diagnostics, metadata graphs or domain sets would violate larger-than-RAM goals.
findings.disposition: Single parent-owned quota-controlled spool, bounded passes and existing root-charged spill sorter/disk membership; borrowed fallible callback with record/byte quotas. Growing 4096-row tiny-run test uses a counting sink. No symbol/error collection in production.

findings.finding: Using mapped/string/finish methods after terminal ingestion failure could replace the original error with closed-metadata state.
findings.disposition: Every public deferred operation checks Writer::open before doing work. Regression exercises all methods and both finish modes after the first failure, verifies no callbacks and preserves the first error through Writer::finish.

findings.finding: Recovery can expose partial callback side effects before a terminal error.
findings.disposition: Reported counters acknowledge successful callbacks only; errors count the failed next row too. Quota, callback and cleanup faults block publication. No automatic replay; caller side effects cannot be rolled back.

limitations: Dependency/group uniqueness scans and journal lookups may be quadratic or worse in metadata/input size. No throughput-parity claim.

Only domain/duplicate errors recover; malformed shapes, foreign/missing IDs, invalid values, I/O, budgets and dependency cycles remain terminal. Direct self-domain supported; alias-to-self and multi-set cycles explicitly unresolved.
Deferred string input uses pre-registered exact labels; automatic dictionary registration remains the separate task-025 phase. Mapped inputs require existing immutable maps.
Logical callback-byte quota excludes caller-selected serialization/allocation; prior callback side effects and tentative accepted rows are not publication or rollback guarantees.
Native coalescing/cutoff behavior deliberately differs from the lossless Rust policy. No native error-number/C-call-state ABI or random retained-list emulation.
Native reference helper runs on Linux under the existing isolated bounds. Four native Rust CI platforms qualify functionality/logical accounting, not OS memory/performance parity.
M3 smoke is regression coverage, not a new larger-than-RAM or M4 OS/RSS/throughput qualification. Task 031 retains those gates. Existing std/path control-allocation limitations remain.
No new dependency, unsafe code, GDX wire-format change, golden/fixture/hash relaxation or frozen-generator change. Tasks 028–031 remain pending.
